SMB (Port 445)
The SMB protocol operates on TCP port 445, and once enabled, you will see the
NetBIOS TCP port 139 is opened as well. The enumeration process of an SMB
protocol should be targeting the following items:
I
I Share names
I
I List of users
I
I List of groups
I
I Domain name
I
I Accounts brute-force
I
I List of SMB vulnerable versions
A quick Nmap scan should reveal some basic information about the target host:

Next, we can run a vulnerability scan using an Nmap script scan to see if
we can get more information (I did not use smb* , because it’s time-consuming
and aggressive):

We will test if the remote host is vulnerable to ms17-010 in Chapter 7. For
the time being, we’re just collecting information. (It could be a false positive;
don’t count on the accuracy of the results that we’re gathering in this phase.)
Note that you can use the smb-enum script option to add more enumeration
outcomes to the results:
root@kali :~ # nmap -sV -p 445 --script=smb-enum 172.16.0.106
If you want to explore more tools for this purpose, then I invite you to try
also the Enum4Linux SMB enumeration utility:
$enum4linux -a [IP address]
